sigma_V.label: FIT, CONDITIONAL ON THE ENGINE (E2.3, v2.1 Phase 2). sigma_V was a FREE parameter of the SMM and is jointly identified with the engine's pull rate (D3 = (b), the option the execution prompt defaults to when the blank is empty), so it is NOT a panel constant: on the same panel and the same moment family Phase 1's estimator C returned 0.01957 [0.01892, 0.02036] and estimator A 0.0205 [0.0197, 0.0213], intervals that do not overlap this one. The value here is conditional on (i) the adopted engine `ar1_fit` and (ii) E3.1's GJR-GARCH-t shape, which was held fixed inside the fit and which Phase 3 re-fits (DECISION_LOG P2-12) -- so sigma_V is EXPECTED TO MOVE AGAIN when Phase 3 changes the volatility block. Quote it as 'sigma_V of the adopted engine', never as 'the panel's sigma_V'. DECISION_LOG P2-8, P2-16.

s_x_fit.label: FIT target for Phase 2, CORRECTED (v2.1 Phase 2, verification V6b): Phase 1 reported 0.1286, which is the calm engine's stationary sd(x) at the REFERENCE half-life of 150 d; e1_2_recovery.smm_fit applies s_x = sbar/0.017*0.1752 whatever half-life it fitted, and the fit returned h = 4.82 d. Re-measured on the fitted process itself: sd(x) = 0.0250 (50 paths x 20,000 d), ACF(1) half-life 4.63 d. This agrees with estimator A's independent 0.0237 [0.0216, 0.0258]. Not a generator parameter, so no path changes.
s_x_fit.interval_note: Phase 1 stored only the percentiles of its 30 bootstrap refits, not the (sbar, h) pairs, so a proper bootstrap interval for the corrected s_x cannot be recomputed from the stored output. The corner range above pairs the endpoints of the sbar and h intervals independently and is therefore WIDER than the true interval; it is reported as a bound, not as an interval.
